title: French India
capsule: French India comprised five non-contiguous enclaves on the Indian subcontinent — Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahé, Yanam, and Chandernagore — with the oldest French establishment at Pondicherry founded in 1674 by François Martin under the French East India Company. The colony's political zenith came under Governor-General Joseph-François Dupleix (1742–1754), who cultivated Indian dynastic clients to extend French influence across the Carnatic; his dismissal and the Seven Years' War (1756–1763) left France with only the five enclave towns. Britain occupied several enclaves during the Napoleonic Wars; sovereignty was formally restored in 1816 but de facto transferred to India in 1954, with a formal treaty of cession signed in 1962.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The five enclave territories are precisely located in colonial administrative records; the dataset's end date of 1848 likely reflects a threshold of effective French control rather than formal sovereignty transfer.
